changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8653-listview-title-retired-rowactiondefs-pinned.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `title` — **retired.** `ListView` resolved its export filename through `schema.label || (schema as any).title`. `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `ListViewSchema` refuses `title` **by name** (`unrecognized_keys: ['title']`) while `ObjectGridPropsSchema` **accepts** it; `packages/types` mirrors the platform contract rather than ruling over it, so declaring `title` on `ListViewSchema` would have made this repo accept what the platform save gate rejects. That asymmetry is also why objectui#6639 could take the *declare* branch for `ObjectGridSchema.title` one package over and this site could not. A parse-based census of `apps/ examples/ content/` and `packages/` found **zero** `list-view` nodes authoring `title`, so the retirement costs no author a filename. Over that same corpus the instrument reports **three** `object-grid` nodes carrying the key: **two authored** ones, both in `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, plus one that is not authored at all — `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` composes `title: schema.table?.title` onto a grid node it builds, so it is a producer writing the key rather than an author declaring it. `ObjectGrid`'s own `title` reads are untouched — they remain declared, ruled and read.

### `.changeset/object-view-unmirrored-keys-7779.md`

- names `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` → `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **What was measured.** Every reading was taken on the `object-view` node renderer (`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, registered by `plugin-view/src/index.tsx`) with `schema.objectName` / `schema.layout` as the positive controls of the same `schema.KEY` query, so each zero is a reading; the repo-wide census of `viewTabBar` finds the key in no source file outside `@object-ui/types` (two doc tables listed it as authorable and are corrected here). The spec side was read through the installed pin (`@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, `ui` entry, 117 exported object schemas walked; control keys `objectName` / `columns` / `navigation` / `listViews` hit): the three spec-modelled keys are optional slots on `ListViewSchema` and `ObjectListViewSchema`; the six local keys have no spec slot anywhere.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `65f1e8dc6` (merge-base with origin/main): 5 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1347 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1920 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36056986517)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `42737c85576c3ecd6e0451c0b7f87d7ac65cea4b`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (107 of 107 at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Head and base.** `head.sha` = `42737c85576c3ecd6e0451c0b7f87d7ac65cea4b` (one commit); merge-base with `origin/main` is `cff4b7754`, the sha the PR says it read. Governing text confirmed in objectui `AGENTS.md` §5 #8: "Corollary: refresh data, don't rebuild UI — after a save/action, invalidate the affected data (`notifyDataChanged` from `@object-ui/react`) so consumers refetch in place; never bump a `key=` to remount a subtree".
- **(a) In-place refetch path per view type, read at head.** plugin-view `ObjectView.tsx`: the non-grid fetch effect's dependency list is `[schema.objectName, dataSource, currentViewType, refreshKey, currentNamedViewConfig, activeViewQueryInputs, renderListView, objectSchemaReady, objectSchema, perms]` and ends in `setData(items)`; `refreshKey` is bumped by the `dataSource.onMutation` subscription (skipped only when a host supplies `renderListView`), `handleDelete`, `handleBulkDelete` and `handleFormSuccess`. `generateViewSchema` emits `object-kanban` / `object-calendar` / `object-gallery` / `object-timeline` / `object-map` / `object-tree`, and `SchemaRenderer` hands the host `data` prop through (its `...props` spread is last; only the AUTHORED `data` key is refused, per the objectui#9571 block). Then, child by child:
  - kanban: registered directly (`'object-kanban': ObjectKanban`); `rawData` reads `externalData` at render, `loading` follows `externalLoading` by effect, own `onMutation` subscription skipped with external data ("Parent handles refresh"). No cached copy.
  - calendar: `ObjectCalendarRenderer` forwards `data={externalData} loading={externalLoading}`; `ObjectCalendar` mirrors by `useEffect(..., [externalData, hasExternalData])` and syncs `loading`. `currentDate`, `view` and `unscheduledOpen` are the component state that now survives, which is the intended outcome, not staleness.
  - gallery: registered directly; `items = props.data || ...` at render, and the fetch effect names `props.data`.
  - timeline: renderer spreads `{...props}`; `rawData = (props as any).data || ...` at render; fetch effect names `(props as any).data`.
  - map: renderer spreads `{...props}`; effect names `dataProp` and does `setData(dataProp)`. `selectedMarkerId` may point at a deleted row, but `selectedMarker = markers.find(...)` and every render site is guarded by `selectedMarker &&`, so the popup closes rather than showing a stale record.
  - tree: renderer spreads `{...props}`; `ObjectTree`'s fetch effect names `(rest as any).data`, so the new array re-issues its own full-record query; expansion `overrides` persist (intended).
  - app-shell `ListView` path: `ListView`'s fetch effect names `schema.refreshTrigger` and its own `refreshKey` (bumped by its `dataSource.onMutation` subscription and the imperative `refresh`); the page sets `fullSchema.refreshTrigger = combinedRefreshKey` (page counter + plugin counter, both monotonic, so the sum moves whenever either does). `ListView` re-seeds `currentView` from `schema.viewType`, `currentSort` from `schema.sort`, `hiddenFields`, `inlineEdit` and `groupingConfig` from the schema by effect, so view edits that used to arrive through the remount still arrive. Children draw `ListView`'s `data`. `ObjectGrid`'s selection is cleared by `resetSelection` on bulk dispatch / delete / dialog close and `selectAllMatching` resets on `hostFindParamsKey`. Stale responses are dropped by `fetchRequestIdRef`.
  - **One observation, not a stale-data regression:** `ListView`'s `pageResetSignature` deliberately excludes the refresh inputs and `serverPage`, so a write that empties a page above 1 (bulk-deleting a whole later page, or a concurrent deleter) leaves the pager on that page with an empty grid and the first-run empty-state copy. The rows shown are the honest result of the requested window, and this is pre-existing `ListView` behaviour (its own `onMutation` refetch, toolbar Refresh and Studio's `renderStudioGridList` already behave so); on this page the remount's reset to page 1 masked it. A clamp belongs in `ListView`, outside this claim's surface; the report does not name it, so the seat should.
- **(b) Kept-remount sets are truthful.** `ObjectGantt`: the registered `object-gantt` renderer destructures `schema` alone and renders `ObjectGantt schema={bound} dataSource={dataSource}` only; `reload` and the fetch effect name `[adapterInputsKey, dataSource, apiFetch, resource, hasInlineData, dataProvider, schema.filter, schema.sort, searchTerm, searchFieldsKey, objectSchema, perms]` with `(rest as any).data intentionally untracked`, no `onMutation`, no `useDataInvalidation`. `ObjectChart`: fetch effect names `[schema.objectName, datasetKey, aggregateKey, filterKey, compareToKey, schema.xAxisKey, schema.chartType, runAggregate, filterScope, fieldOptionLabel]`, no refresh input, ignores host rows. `ObjectGrid`: fetch effect ends `..., dataConfig, refreshKey, perms.isLoaded, groupingProjectionKey]` where `refreshKey` is its internal counter; no `onMutation`, `refreshTrigger` or bus read. Whitelist check: `reachableVisualizations = [fullSchema.viewType, ...(fullSchema.appearance?.allowedVisualizations ?? [])]` reads the same `appearance` the page hands `ListView`; `ListView` draws its switcher only when `showViewSwitcher` is set AND `availableViews` has more than one entry, this page sets `showViewSwitcher` only when `allowedVisualizations` has more than one entry, and the localStorage "saved view" restore in `ListView` is commented out, so with no whitelist no user can reach a gantt or chart visualization in this list. The check is conservative (remounts even when the whitelisted entry does not resolve), which the PR states. Both constants' docstrings name the two members, the reason each has no in-place path, the grid branch (plugin-view), and a ⛔ do-not-drop note; `REMOUNT_TO_REFRESH_VISUALIZATIONS` also explains why `chart` is about the in-list switcher on this page.
- **(c) Double fetch.** After a data-source write on the page, `ListView`'s own `onMutation` bump and `refreshTrigger` are two deps of one effect: one run if they land in the same commit, otherwise two, with the older response discarded by the stale-request guard; `ObjectStackAdapter.find` keeps an `inflightFinds` map keyed by resource + `stableStringify(params)` and returns the existing promise, so concurrent identical reads are one round trip (the claim in `ListView`'s comment holds for that adapter). On base the same write produced an `onMutation` refetch on the doomed instance plus a full mount fetch on the new one, so this is not a regression. On the plugin-view standalone path the parent's subscription is the only bump (children skip theirs with external data): one fetch.
- **(d) Pins.** plugin-view pin: 9 tests (6 in-place via `it.each`, each asserting (a) same `data-instance` from a `useState` initializer and (b) `data-rows` reaching 2 after `find` is called twice; 3 remount cases asserting a fresh instance; `ObjectGrid` mocked with the same stand-in). app-shell pin: 4 tests on the real page, plugin `ObjectView` and `ListView` (2 in-place: `listQueries` delta exactly 1 and the `view-description` node, which `ListView` renders, is the same node; 2 remount: own type gantt, gantt in whitelist).
